eligible_license.note: Inspected License.txt: it is the BSD-3-Clause-LBNL variant, including LBNL’s standard additional default enhancement license clause. SPDX lists BSD-3-Clause-LBNL as OSI-approved; Legal.txt separately records DOE government rights and provenance.

primary_evidence.note: The official Warp manual provides the source/download, installation, and user documentation; it states example simulation scripts are employed in a U.S. Particle Accelerator School course. The official publications page identifies peer-reviewed code and application literature: https://warp.lbl.gov/home/publications-and-documentation.

product_identity: Warp — Python particle-in-cell simulation framework for plasma and high-current accelerator beams
agency: U.S. Department of Energy — Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory
status_notes: Canonical repository: https://bitbucket.org/berkeleylab/warp. Active source history; last inspected change 2026-09-01. License-bearing history dates to 2013-04-22.

source_rows.metadata_screen_reason: DOE CODE reports a named license claim; this is a discovery screen only and does not establish an OSI-approved or source-confirmed license.

decision_reason: TraVerSE is a separately installable Python toolkit with detailed installation and usage documentation, a source-verified BSD-3-Clause-LBNL grant, and LBNL/DOE funding attribution. However, the current public source branch has had no code change since 2019-05-08, and this review found no current official distribution/support statement, operational deployment, or independent documented scientific use. Hold rather than admit it; its age alone does not establish the exceptional historical notability needed for an Archived record.

government_provenance.note: The repository’s own copyright/license text assigns rights to the Regents through Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, says DOE funding supported the software, and grants federal government rights; setup.py also identifies a lbl.gov author email.

public_source.note: The public repository exposes the Python toolkit, package setup, tests, requirements, and substantial user/installation guidance without credentials.

eligible_license.note: Inspected the actual grant: it is the permissive BSD-3-Clause-LBNL variant with the standard enhancement clause, which is listed by SPDX as OSI-approved.

primary_evidence.note: The README describes a usable trajectory-error-flagging toolkit and gives installation/use instructions, but this review found no product page, versioned release history beyond setup.py’s 1.0.0, deployed service, cited scientific use, or current support evidence. The latest source change inspected is 2019-05-08, so maturity is present but notability/current use remains unresolved.

product_identity: TraVerSE — Python toolkit for detecting simple errors in GPS trajectory traces
agency: U.S. Department of Energy — Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory
status_notes: Latest inspected code change: 2019-05-08. Product packaging/docs exist, but no current-use or sufficient notability evidence was located; do not mark Archived absent an unusual historical-significance case.
